h1: Plot Generator: Random Story and Video Ideas in One Click

sections.h: How to turn a premise into a script
body: A generated premise is a starting point, not a script. Turn it into three beats, then match the length to the format it suggests.

ol: Hook: open on the hero already chasing what they want, and show the obstacle in the first few seconds.
Turn: make the obstacle bigger twice, each time forcing the hero to try something new.
Payoff: reveal the twist so it changes what the goal meant, and end on a line or image that lands.
Fit the format: a 30 to 60 second short needs one turn and a punchline; a short drama episode needs a reversal mid-way and a cliffhanger; a stage skit can escalate the same game three times.
Write the dialogue in short spoken lines and read it aloud before filming.

ul: Re-roll one part at a time: keep the hero you like and change only the obstacle until it clicks.
Combine two premises: the hero from one roll and the twist from another often make the strangest stories.
Keep what surprises you. If a combination sounds odd, ask what would make it true; that is usually your story.
Swap the setting for a place you can actually film, like your kitchen or a park, and keep the rest.
Change the genre on purpose: play a horror-sounding premise as a comedy, or a silly one completely straight.
Give the hero a name and one habit before you write a line, so they feel like a person.

faq.q: Can I use generated ideas for my channel or a competition?
faq.a: Yes. The combinations are yours to use however you like, including on monetised channels. If you also use one of our scripts, credit Script: cv.cm under CC BY 4.0.

faq.q: Some combinations do not make sense. Is that a bug?
faq.a: Every combination is grammatical, but not every one is a good story. Re-roll the part that does not fit, or treat the odd pairing as a challenge to make it work.

faq.q: How do I make a premise work for a group of five?
faq.a: Give each extra person a role around the hero: the rival, the helper, the person who knows the twist, and someone who makes the obstacle worse. Pick the 5-minute stage skit format.
